credit_frameworks.title: The Frameworks for Higher Education Qualifications of UK Degree-Awarding Bodies (second edition, February 2024)
credit_frameworks.issuer: Quality Assurance Agency for Higher Education (QAA)

statements.fact: One credit equals 10 notional hours of learning
statements.quote: The various credit frameworks used within the UK operate according to the same underpinning principles (for example, one credit equates to 10 notional hours of learning).

statements.fact: The FHEQ itself is not a credit framework; England uses the QAA credit framework of 2021
statements.quote: The FHEQ is a qualifications framework, based on the outcomes represented by the main qualification titles. It is not an integrated credit and qualifications framework, nor is its use dependent on credit. ... A revised higher education credit framework for England was published by QAA in 2021, and all degree-awarding bodies in England and Northern Ireland that award credit are able to reference this framework as it is designed to be complementary to the FHEQ.

statements.fact: Scotland and Wales use integrated credit frameworks (SCQF, CQFW)
statements.quote: The SCQF and the CQFW are integrated credit and qualifications frameworks which means that they specify minimum credit volumes and levels for qualifications

statements.fact: Bachelor’s with honours: three or four full-time years
statements.quote: Bachelor's degrees with honours form the largest group of higher education qualifications. Typically, learning outcomes for these courses would be expected to be achieved on the basis of study equivalent to three or four full-time academic years and lead to qualifications with titles such as Bachelor of Arts, BA (Hons) or Bachelor of Science, BSc (Hons).

credit_frameworks.title: Higher Education Credit Framework for England: Advice on Academic Credit Arrangements (2021)

statements.fact: One credit = 10 notional hours
statements.quote: Credit value The number of credits, at a particular level, assigned to a body of learning. The number of credits is based on the estimated learning hours (where one credit typically represents 10 notional hours of learning).

statements.fact: Notional learning hours definition
statements.quote: Notional learning hours The number of hours which it is expected that a learner (at a particular level) will spend, on average, to achieve the specified learning outcomes at that level. This may include time spent in class, directed learning, independent study and assessment. One credit is typically described as being equal to 10 hours of notional learning.

statements.fact: A 20-credit module equals 200 hours
statements.quote: Credit assigned to modules or courses is based on the approximate number of hours a learner is expected to spend learning to achieve the learning outcomes for that module, including guided and independent study. For example, a 20-credit module equates to 200 hrs, divided into different modes of learning.

statements.fact: Bachelor’s with honours: 360 credits, 90 at level 6; first cycle, 180-240 ECTS
statements.quote: Bachelor’s degrees with honours (eg BA/BSc Hons) | FHEQ Level 6 | Minimum credit 360 (90 at FHEQ level 6) | First cycle (end of cycle) qualifications | 180-240 ECTS credits
statements.location: Credit Framework for England 2021 table, p. 8 [PDF p. 10]; table cells joined with | by the collector

statements.fact: Values in the table are minimums

statements.fact: 120 credits in a typical academic year

statements.fact: Two UK credits = one ECTS credit; 60 ECTS = one full-time year
statements.quote: ECTS is based on the principle that 60 ECTS credits are equivalent to the learning outcomes and associated workload of a typical full-time academic year of formal learning. In everyday practice, two UK credits are equivalent to one ECTS credit.

statements.fact: A 360-credit honours degree equates to 180 ECTS
statements.quote: For example, a bachelor’s degrees with honours in England, Wales and Northern Ireland, with a typical total volume of at least 360 credits, equate to 180 ECTS credits as long as the learning outcomes are consistent with the relevant Dublin descriptor.
